question: Can native TimeSeries ID membership use an exact right-side IN-set/semi-filter with lower CPU and bounded RSS than BOTH ALL and ANY JOIN, across duplicate density and label/time selectors?
baseline: Generated native TAGS ALL LEFT TimeRanges membership SQL in unchanged pinned O1 join-override ClickHouse; secondary R30 ANY as comparison.
candidate: Rewrite only internal diagnostic generated SQL from LEFT JOIN right rows + matched flag to correlated ID IN (identical right SELECT id); retain original unmatched ID-range OR expression. No production source mutation.
fixture: Reuse deterministic repeated stable-ID plus before/after-window control, at k=1 and k=16; exact SHA and physical parts logged by isolated CI.
single_variable: At each frozen physical table compare ALL vs ANY vs explicit IN-set semantic filter on the same TAGS/TimeRanges data, same query columns/settings, run A/B/C/C/B/A.
math_bound: When all right matching rows expose matched=1, existence of a right row is equivalent to id IN (rightSELECT id) for each TAGS ID, and the metric-range exclusion fallback is identical. IN materializes a set of up to #unique matching right IDs, but its implementation and memory are not bounded by EXPLAIN estimates. Do not assume improved RSS.
falsifier: Any missing/mismatched IDs, (id,samples) or side-effect tag grouping; unsupported IN syntax/typing; worse CPU/memory at both density levels; over-limit RSS/OOM; unbounded planner cost or alias capture.
test_matrix: Exact rewrite source parser unit tests; one isolated 4096 ID fixture at k=1 and k=16 with disjoint before/after-window cohorts; stage/project/whole selectors, explicit ID-sets and SAMPLES array parity, plans, ALL/ANY/IN mirrored phases for project, QueryFinish CPU/wall/tracker and actual physical counts; later full patched C++ native PromQL oracle, 1/4/8 clients, 14d if positive.
runner_budget: One isolated Ubuntu Actions no-build job using existing SHA-verified O1 binary, 2 tables, bounded series and max_memory_usage<=2GiB; do not interrupt E01 R29 compilation.
